headline: Oil eases from $100 and ceasefires firm up, but a Canadian rate hike is now likely
summary: After touching $100, the odds of oil running to $105 fell 10 pts and US–Iran ceasefire odds bounced. Canada's central bank is now 72% likely to raise rates next week. Big money is fighting over the US midterms, Google pulled ahead in the AI model race, and Bolsonaro regained ground four days before Brazil votes.

takeaways.lead: Oil is taking a breather after $100.
takeaways.text: WTI reaching $105 this month fell 10 pts in a day to 47.5%, and $110 fell 6 to 18.5%. The US–Iran ceasefire bounced: through Oct 31 is 81.5% (up 3), and through Oct 28 is 85.5% (up 4). An Iran–Oman Hormuz management deal by Nov 30 rose 6 pts to 27%.

takeaways.lead: Canada will probably raise rates next week.
takeaways.text: A Bank of Canada hike on Oct 28 jumped another 19 pts to 72% (up 56 this week; $375k market). The US Fed is still expected to hold on Oct 29 (88.5%, up 3) but hike in December (77.5%).

takeaways.lead: Whales are battling over the midterms.
takeaways.text: One trader put $50k on a Republican sweep at just 9¢ (a long-shot bet that pays about 11x). Others put about $70k on a Democratic sweep (63.5%). There's also $50k on Republicans winning Texas's Senate seat, and Democrat Amy Acton jumped 7 pts to 78.5% for Ohio governor.

takeaways.lead: Google is pulling ahead in AI.
takeaways.text: Google as the best AI model at the end of October rose 9 pts to 82% ($3M market), and Anthropic fell 8 to 15%. Anthropic's next model (Fable 5.2) by Oct 24 dropped 27 pts to 17% (thin market). OpenAI reaching a $1.25T valuation by year-end is 93.5% (up 11).

takeaways.lead: Bolsonaro regained ground before Sunday's vote.
takeaways.text: Flávio Bolsonaro rose 4 pts to 80%, and Lula fell 3 to 19.5%. About $93k of large bets went his way (including $41k against Lula) versus about $32k against him.

Two traders sold $48k of 'no hantavirus pandemic in 2026', a quiet bet that the risk is higher than the market's 2.4%. It's still very unlikely, but worth noticing. Separately, FDA approval of a skin cancer vaccine by end-2027 fell 14 pts to 52.5% (thin $193k market).

sections.title: What's new today
bullets: Odds of a French state of emergency by year-end fell 4 pts to 13% ($203k market), so the unrest scare is easing.
Russia capturing the Ukrainian town of Vodianske by year-end rose 6 pts to 39% (thin market). Peace talks by Dec 31 also rose 7 pts to 43.5%, so fighting and talking are both priced up.
Toronto's mayoral race is tightening: Brad Bradford rose 10 pts to 35.5% against Olivia Chow's 64.5%.

sections.title: Trading signals
bullets: Oil: $100 is done; $105 this month 47.5% (down 10), $110 18.5%. A pullback is likely if ceasefire headlines keep improving.
Rates: Canada hike 72%, Fed hold 88.5%, Fed December hike 77.5%. A $22k bet said the Fed won't cut in October.
Largest company at year-end: Nvidia 74.5% (up 3), Apple 19.8% (down 6).
Gold: a $16k bet said gold won't hit $6,000 by December.

sections.title: Wars & geopolitics
bullets: US–Iran ceasefire through Oct 31: 81.5% (up 3); Israel–Iran through Nov 30: 60.5% (flat).
About $34k of large bets went on no Iran leadership change by year-end, and $13k on Hormuz traffic not returning to normal.
Xi meeting Japan's PM Takaichi by year-end rose 6 pts to 77%, a sign of easing China–Japan tension.

sections.title: Elections that move markets
bullets: Israel (Oct 27): Eizenkot 51.5% (up 2), Netanyahu 27.5% (down 2). A $25k bet said Likud won't get 30–34 seats.
US midterms (Nov 3): Democrats take both chambers 63.5%; Democrats win the House about 92%. Ohio governor: Acton (D) 78.5%.

sections.title: Everyday life
bullets: Gas: oil touched $100 but is easing. Pump prices may plateau if the ceasefires hold.
Canadians with variable mortgages: a hike next week is now 72% likely.
US loans: no Fed cut is coming this year; a December hike is 77.5% likely.
